blocks.html: DECISION 2  Four features are ON that the engine leaves OFF. Which way do you want them?

The situation. Four gates are engine-default-OFF, and both routes onto your screen turn them ON: the launcher declares defaultVal "1" for them and applies it unconditionally, and every install on disk carries a launcher_env.json holding the same four, which the engine applies to any variable you have not set yourself. So in practice you have never seen these four off, and nothing was labelled to tell you.

rows.html: Prop specular. Changes how every building reads.
Prop hemisphere ambient. Sits directly on your “props look dark” report.
Its row also labelled the gate “default ON” — a copy of the exact false claim that had to be deleted from the engine source. The label is now corrected.

The worst of the four. A second reader (visual_tuning_profile.cpp:182) is a pure presence test, so setting the variable to anything — “0” included — suppresses the per-mission water art direction from data/visual_tuning.json. Every launcher launch trips it.

blocks.html: Correction — this page told you an hour ago that “a launcher launch runs these four ON while a shell or batch launch runs them OFF”. That is wrong, and I wrote it. I took it from the comment in mc2_launcher.cpp, which is also wrong. The .bat route sets MC2_NO_LAUNCHER=1, and that is precisely the branch on which the engine reads launcher_env.json itself (gameosmain.cpp:1091). Both routes give you the four ON. The only ways to get them off are to set them to 0 yourself, or to set MC2_LAUNCHER_ENV_JSON=0.
2a.  The one that is a defect, not a preference

MC2_WATER_SKYTINT should be decided on its own, and it is not a taste call. A second reader (visual_tuning_profile.cpp:182) is a pure presence test: if (!envIsSet("MC2_WATER_SKYTINT")). So the variable being set to anything — including "0" — suppresses the per-mission waterSkyTintStrength that data/visual_tuning.json authors. Turning it “off” by writing 0 does not restore the authored art; it silences it. This one wants to be unset, not zeroed, and bundling it with three preference questions — as this page did an hour ago — forces you to answer a bug and three matters of taste with a single yes.
2b.  The three that are genuine judgement calls
MC2_STATIC_PROP_PBR_V1, MC2_STATIC_PROP_AMBIENT_V1 and MC2_CLOUD_SHADOW are preferences. There are three ways to settle them, not the two this page offered:

rows.html:
(a) Make the launcher agree with the engine
flip defaultVal to unset
You decide these three are not wanted by default. Launcher, shell and engine finally say the same thing.

It does not heal a single install you already have. LoadEnvJson seeds from defaultVal and then overwrites from the on-disk JSON (mc2_launcher.cpp:805-836), so every existing launcher_env.json keeps its "1". The flip only affects a fresh install with no JSON. Fixing what is on your disk is a separate, manual step.

(b) Make the engine agree with the launcher
flip the ENGINE defaults ON
You decide these three are wanted — which is what you have actually been playing with all along. The launcher stops being a lie by becoming right.

A real default-behaviour change for anyone who is not you, and it needs the same eyes-on grading as any default flip. This option was missing when the decision was put to you, which made the choice look narrower than it is.
(c) Keep the split, now that it is labelled
Treat the launcher as a deliberate preset. The rows now read (engine OFF; launcher ON) instead of claiming the engine default.
Cheapest and already true. But AB-0 keeps not being a default frame, so every absolute judgement on this page needs the MC2_LAUNCHER_ENV_JSON=0 caveat forever.

rows.html: Why it is yours / what moved

Shoreline: DISPLACEMENT, FACETING, or the third thing?
still a one-word answer — but the question has changed since it was first written

Look at the mc2_17 waterline and say which you are seeing. (a) DISPLACEMENT — the edge is in the wrong place, cutting across land or sea. (b) FACETING — the edge is in the right place but built from visible straight risers instead of a curve. (c) A GLOW TRACING THE TILE GRID — the edge itself is fine, but something bright is drawn along it in steps, worst at night.
You can answer (a) vs (b) from the two plots in §20a without launching anything: they draw the stock waterline against the 128 wu tile lattice for both maps. On mc2_17 the stock line is a smooth sinuous curve that crosses tile boundaries freely; on mc2_10 it is a right-angle staircase locked to the lattice. If what you see on mc2_17 looks like the mc2_10 plot, that is displacement and the offline data is wrong about the map. Caveat stated plainly: those are offline contour plots of the shipping heightfield, not rendered frames — no rendered engine frame of mc2_17 water exists anywhere on disk.

Two corrections since this row was written, and the second one is a live lead.
(1) The arithmetic that used to appear here is withdrawn. This row previously said “the arithmetic says (b): a 128 wu tile projects to ~147 px at the intro camera and you measured risers of 138–148 px”. That px pair has no derivation anywhere in the repo — no script, no measurement JSON, no status doc — and an identical “137–148px” string does exist, in tools/visual_verify/regions/mc2_10_saved_204523.json, describing mc2_10 at a top-down pose. It was most likely re-attributed to mc2_17. A number that may belong to the other map must not be allowed to pick your answer, so it has been removed rather than repeated.
(2) A default-ON candidate cause that all six shoreline lanes missed. MC2_TERRAIN_SHORELINE has three readers and they disagree: gos_terrain_lod_chunk.cpp:2659 and mclib/terrain.cpp:1120 both read !(v && v[0]=='0') → default ON, while gos_TerrainLodChunk_IsShorelineMaskActive() at gos_terrain_lod_chunk.cpp:3903 reads (v && v[0] && v[0]!='0') → default OFF. That third reader is the one that suppresses the legacy screen-space runShoreline() pass (gos_postprocess.cpp:3404). Because it is false on an unset environment, the suppression never fires and the legacy glow runs on every stock frame with water, alongside the V3 band it was supposed to replace. The engine’s own comment at :2659 says that legacy pass “traced the raw tile-quantized water-mesh edge and amplified the staircase at night”. Chain re-verified end to end for this page. If your answer is (c), that is where the fix is, and it is a one-line change.

Flat lighting is measured as unable to close the gap — the runway is bit-identical across all four strength arms. What is left is an albedo change, the class you rejected twice as “WAY worse”. The proposal would be a narrower, concrete-only albedo arm. Yes, no, or close the item.

But it is UNTRACKED in git and has never been proven in a live run — a clean checkout loses it, and the hook stays armed until it is proven. DEFAULT-LAUNCH REALITY — what you actually get if you launch and change nothing. In short: the crash and the shadow and night-clipping fixes ship; most of the look work does not, and is waiting on the gradings above.

blocks.html: NO CODE CHANGE WAS NEEDED â€” and none was made. Both mechanisms were already shipped and simply switched off. Root cause is three stacked things: (1) static_prop.frag writes the a=0.25 "no self shadow" GBuffer class and shadow_screen.frag deliberately skips the dynamic cascade for it ("CPU never self-shadowed buildings"); (2) the baked base light is a per-LEAF constant (GetARGBHighlight(), one scalar per TG_Shape), so it adds no intra-surface variation, and calc_light has no occlusion term at all; (3) what is left is a pure per-face max(N·L,0) â€” precisely "fully lit or dark, nothing between". Props already cast into the CSM cascades, so no caster-set widening was required and the alpha-card foliage exclusion was never touched.

Why BOTH gates. MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE opts props back into the dynamic cascade â€” that gives coarse wing-on-wing shadow, but the cascades are map-sized and cannot resolve a doorway reveal. MC2_SSAO adds the fine contact term (recesses, inside corners, undersides) using depth + GBuffer normals props already write. Measured on mc2_01 day: RECEIVE alone changes 0.25-0.73% of pixels and 100% of them get DARKER, zero brighter (a pure occlusion term can only darken â€” animation or a lighting bug could not be one-sided); adding SSAO multiplies coverage 20-60x (to 1.5-14.7%) while staying ~99% darker.

blocks.html: Root cause. The min-screen-size clamp added by f412423e was max(1.0, kLbMinNdc / sil) with no upper bound. sil falls off as 1/distance, so k grew without limit and pinned every fixture to a constant hard-edged bright block at every camera distance. Holding a constant screen size was the clamp's literal intent — correct at playable RTS range, which is what made the lights visible at grazing angles — but past that range several hundred regularly-spaced fixtures simply never shrink. Regular spacing + constant size = the dashes. A secondary error compounded it ~1.5x: kLbRefRadius was the authored top-cap radius (0.8), but the rigid billboard maps local Z (the 2.85-unit post axis) onto toCam, so the post foreshortens and the viewer actually sees the local XY cross-section (runwaylight.ase extents 2.015 x 2.326, radius ~1.2). The clamp was sizing against a feature that is never on screen.

blocks.html: (a) Concrete patchwork — REJECTED ARM, KEPT FOR THE RECORD ONLY. The A/B below is the pair you graded “WAY worse”. It is retained as evidence of what was tried and refused, not as a recommendation. Read the “AFTER” panel as the rejected outcome. The patchwork it targets remains unfixed. The cement catalog packs concrete from several authored families at materially different base tone, and cement is flat-lit by design (terrain_lod_chunk.frag forces normalLight = mix(normalLight, 1.0, pureConcrete)), so no shared lighting term unifies them and the raw tone difference shows at full contrast with straight tile-boundary seams. MC2_CEMENT_TONE_MATCH normalises each cell's [P50,P90] concrete band to the atlas median per channel. Measured on this map: cells=110 adjusted=96 ref_rgb=149.0,146.4,138.4; between-family luminance stddev 9.03 → 3.95.

blocks.html: (b) Missing road swaths — honest partial. PopulateRecipeCementWords bakes a cement word for a TRANSITION tile only when a corner terrainType resolves to a SOLID cement layer and a corner mask derives. A road crossing open ground satisfies neither, bakes no word, and falls back to the bare baked colormap. Census on this map: transition_baked=512 dropped_no_layer=266 — 266 of 778 transition tiles (34%) draw no paving at all. MC2_CEMENT_TRANSITION_FALLBACK lets a dropped tile adopt an orthogonally adjacent tile's layer, but recovers only 33 of 266 (12%), because dropped tiles form contiguous runs so there is usually no neighbour carrying a word to borrow from. Do not read this as "roads fixed" — it stays default OFF. The real fix is upstream: admit alpha/transition cement slots into the catalog atlas (drop the isAlpha skip in BuildCementCatalogAtlas, give each transition slot its own layer, honour cell alpha in the frag). That is a genuine slice and is not landed.

blocks.html: (c) The runway/apron tone split — re-diagnosed, and it is NOT an art-tone problem. User verdict on mc2_10: "I don't understand why the runway under the plane is grey when it is black on top of the concrete." A new always-on census [CEMENT_CELL_TONE v1] reports every catalog cell's concrete-band tone. On mc2_10: cells=19 usable=19 median_lum=147.2 dark_cells=0. On mc2_24: cells=110 usable=110 median_lum=146.3 dark_cells=0. Neither map has a dark asphalt family at all — so no atlas-side tone fix can reach that runway, and the original "normalise the asphalt family to the concrete family" theory is disproven.

The class view settles it. Sampled luminance in the mc2_10 beauty frame: apron concrete 145.1–171.3, runway under the parked aircraft 65.0, bare terrain 54.3. The runway sits at terrain brightness because it is terrain: the diag shows it uncoloured, i.e. baked colormap only, never cement-classified, drawn through the full lighting term — while the apron beside it is cement-atlas art that is lighting-exempt by construction. Two sources, one of them ignoring the scene light. That single mechanism explains all three of the user's observations in that frame: the tone change along one runway, the missing pavement (same dropped-transition census: dropped_no_layer=278 of 320 on mc2_10 — 87%), and the mismatched edge strip where colormap meets cement.

blocks.html: ⚠ Caveat on the class-diag as an instrument. A tile carrying a paved &Overlays id (PAVED_ROAD, RUNWAY, …) laid over a non-cement base is never cement-classified at all: it never reaches the transition branch and increments no drop counter, so it is absent from the drop denominator entirely. The class view still colours some of those tiles, so it can read as “classified” where the census says nothing was baked. Your annotation on this pose was correct and the instrument was partly misleading you. The always-on [CEMENT_TRANSITION_DROP v1] census plus the new opt-in [CEMENT_PAVEMENT_GAP v1] census (MC2_TERRAIN_LOD_CHUNK_DIAG=524288) together give the true numerator and denominator. No classifier predicate change exists on any branch — that lane was cancelled.

Fix landed for (c), not yet verified. MC2_CEMENT_LIT (0..1, default 0.0) lerps cement back into the terrain's own lighting term, so apron and colormap-runway share one light and hold a consistent relationship under sun, dusk and night. At 0.0 the expression collapses to the historical flat-lit slab and is bit-identical to stock. Caveat, recorded honestly: the ON arm has NOT been captured. Parallel lanes committed into the shared worktree mid-session, so a clean-fingerprint build of that commit could not be produced and it was not deployed. The diagnosis above is fully evidenced from the clean 608dea4d exe; the cure is not. It needs a quiet worktree before it can be recommended.
